build.//: Three profiles. `development` is what you iterate in; `preview` is the internal-test build that goes to TestFlight and Play internal testing; `production` is the store build, which nothing in Phase 3 submits.
build.//env: Only EXPO_PUBLIC_BUILD_PROFILE is set here. The client ids and the API base URL are NOT, and deliberately: they are gitignored (mobile/.env), so a cloud build cannot see them and putting them here would put them back in git — the thing keeping them out of it was for. Register them once as EAS environment variables instead: `npx eas-cli env:create --name EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID --value <id> --visibility plaintext --environment preview` (and the same for the Android id and EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL). Skip this and the build succeeds and installs, and the app shows NOT CONFIGURED on the sign-in screen — a twenty-minute round trip for a missing variable.

development.//: A DEVELOPMENT BUILD, not Expo Go. Expo Go cannot host expo-secure-store's keystore access or a native Google sign-in bound to this app's bundle id — testing items 2, 3 and 4 in Expo Go would prove nothing about the real app.

preview.//: The real-device test build. iOS goes to TestFlight, Android to Play internal testing or a direct APK install. Signed with the same EAS-managed keystore as production on Android, which is why the SHA-1 registered in Google Cloud Console covers both. No `channel` here: channels route OTA updates and need expo-updates, which is not installed — declaring one would fail the build with a message about update channels rather than about the missing package.

production.//: Store builds. Nothing in Phase 3 submits, and `eas submit` is deliberately not configured below. No `channel` — see the preview profile.
